results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 72 body-unit summaries match the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p76, with p58 in Channels and p37-p38 after Attribution as the spec places them). The five callouts are opening apparatus and match no spec paragraph. The two units the outliner marked as holding two ideas (p32, p64) are summarised with exactly the two parts their spec controlling ideas name.

results.quote: Kleinanzeigen's safety page warns users that "Kleinanzeigen" messages inside the chat can be written by the chat partner
results.finding: The outliner marked this unit as two ideas ('operators moving safety checks earlier / platform brand in messages as a risk signal'). The last sentence is a separate claim (the platform's own brand as a risk signal), not evidence that operators decide earlier. The spec's controlling idea for p32 itself joins the two claims with 'and', so the draft follows the spec; the draft could only soften it by presenting the brand point as one of the early signals. The root is the spec bundling two claims in one paragraph.

Trade-offs ¶1 (p64), also marked two_ideas: the framing sentence ('Veldmark's decisions are not the only right answers') is a lead-in to the table and 'Of these, masking needs the most care' subordinates the masking discussion to it, so the paragraph has one controlling idea (masking as the trade-off that needs most care). The placement problem of the framing sentence is recorded under transition_expresses_declared_relationship. No other unit was marked.

Every unit advances a supporting claim S1-S6 or the introduction/conclusion; the Artemis monitoring paragraph (p53) supports S5/S6 (measure the contact path) even though its placement is questioned under flow.

Each table is introduced or followed by text saying what it shows (concept contrast p12, channels p14 with four observations, components p19 with the two boundaries, gate checks p33, retention p37/p38 'The last row is the reason', delivery p47/p48, baseline p59 now states what the baseline shows, trade-offs p64, verticals p65). Figures 1-6 carry captions and are used in the text (Figure 4 by p44, Figure 6 by p62). Quotations (OLX, Discord, Autotrader, Rightmove, CarGurus, Zillow, CoStar, Adevinta, Ofcom, EECC) are each followed by the point they make.

results.quote: Veldmark's decisions are not the only right answers: the table sets two options against each other for six choices and says when each is right.
results.finding: Declared transition_in for the Trade-offs section is contrast, start_of_this, carrying over Veldmark's decisions and introducing when the other option is right. In the draft the section opens with the six-row table, and the contrast sentence comes only after it, so at the boundary from the worked example's decisions the reader meets the table with no transition. Flow reader A (A8) reports the same: 'It would work better before the table.' Move the sentence (or its first clause) above the table.

All other transition_in entries are expressed at their boundaries: e.g. p08 contrast ('The second case was a counting problem, not a safety problem'), p11 problem_solution ('Ingrid's second question, what a lead is, needs definitions first'), p18 ('Whatever the channel'), p27 contrast ('not a busy thread ... It is the busy inbox'), p29 contrast, p30 problem_solution ('The step between stored and shown is where Veldmark put the message safety gate'), p37 sequence ('Both objects leave data behind'), p38 cause_effect ('The last row is the reason'), p39 contrast ('With the conversation and its gate in place, the chapter turns to the other object'), p42/p50/p63 conclusion_summary, p59 problem_solution (the forum Ingrid took her questions to adopts the design), p68 problem_solution ('The eight failure modes above point to decisions'), p74, p75, p76.

results.quote: Lead counts are also an operational signal: a broken contact button looks like a quiet day unless someone watches lead counts per platform, channel and country against a forecast. [...] It is about monitoring, not about matching leads to outcomes or about users leaving the platform. It reads like an aside dropped into the middle of the section. (flowB B1)
results.finding: Both flow readers lost the thread at the same paragraph: A5 'It is about monitoring and has nothing to do with attribution, so it felt out of place'; B1 'reads like an aside dropped into the middle of the section'. Both propose moving it to Failure Modes or the Chief Architect's 'Measure the path' metrics. The draft states the declared additional_support relationship ('also'), so the difficulty is the position the spec gives p53 inside Attribution, between the attribution and disintermediation paragraphs. Overall, both readers describe the declared organising principle (follow one contact through its life, conversation then lead, then replay and generalise) and mark no section unclear.

results.quote: Even "immutable" messages carry metadata that changes, and that shapes the store.
results.finding: Both flow readers stopped on the same opener: it repeats the last sentence of p24 ('messages are immutable in content but their metadata changes'). A3: 'The repetition made me pause to check whether something new was being said. Nothing was.' B7: 'a small stutter, not a loss of thread.' The declared transition (example, carrying over mutable metadata) can be made by pointing forward instead of restating, e.g. opening on OLX's post as the example of that changing metadata shaping the store.

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: One Messaging Platform, Four Brands ¶4
results.quote: That gives 13 + 1 + 5 = **19 leads** from the 23 contacts that Motorvane's 2027 reporting counted as leads; the other four were repeat contacts from the same buyers.
results.finding: Both readers re-read this sentence: the relative clause 'that Motorvane's 2027 reporting counted as leads' reads at first as attaching to the 19 rather than the 23 (A7, B3), and A7 had to re-check the arithmetic. Split it: Motorvane's 2027 reporting counted all 23 contacts as leads; under the rule they make 19, and the other four are repeat contacts (second e-mail, merged booking, two repeat calls).

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: One Messaging Platform, Four Brands ¶1
results.quote: The "Common Ground program" and Keybridge are not introduced in this chapter. I worked out from the table that Keybridge is an agency-software business inside the group, but only after reading the table. (flowA A6; also A1: "Four systems are announced, but this section describes only Tradeyard and Motorvane.")
results.finding: Both cold readers could not tell what Veldmark's 'four contact systems' (p05) are until the baseline table, and met Keybridge as 'the fourth' without knowing why a software vendor counts as a contact system (A1, A6; B4). The spec's audience already knows Veldmark's brands, Keybridge and Common Ground, so this is low-stakes for the intended reader, but the chapter's own count is announced in p05 and resolved only in p59; the same mismatch was raised by a single reader last round. Cheap fix in the draft: name the four (Tradeyard, Motorvane, Hearthly, and Keybridge on the receiving side) where p05 first says 'four contact systems'.

results.quote: This sentence explains how to read the Trade-offs table, but it comes after the table. I had already read the table without that framing. It would work better before the table. (flowA A8)
results.finding: Single reader. Same placement problem as the transition result for p64; fixing that fixes this.

results.quote: which professional entity (dealer, rooftop, meaning one dealer location, agency branch, individual agent)
results.finding: Single reader (A2): the gloss 'meaning one dealer location' inside a comma list reads as a list item. Use parentheses or a dash for the gloss.

results.quote: Messaging is a natural client of the group identity ([[identity-and-verification]]), and the little that marketplaces publish about messaging and lead architecture points the same way.
results.finding: Single reader (A10): 'the same way' must refer back to the heading, but the first clause is about identity, so the direction the evidence points in is unclear. Say 'points towards sharing it' or similar.

results.quote: So the section steps back to the first object without saying so. The link "the other side of attribution" is asserted rather than shown, and I had to think about why the topic sits here. (flowB B2)
results.finding: Single reader (B2; a single reader raised the same link last round): disintermediation is mostly about the conversation and channels, and its place in the Attribution section is asserted. The difficulty comes from the spec's placement; the draft could say in one clause that leakage is the contacts whose outcomes the portal never sees.

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: One Messaging Platform, Four Brands ¶2
results.quote: the volume figures arrive late. The safety section had already used "about 14 million messages a day" to argue the LLM cost point, and had already set the 150 ms budget, so these capacity numbers feel like a delayed justification for decisions already described. (flowB B5)

results.finding: Single reader (B6): the sentence leads with the sixteen minutes, which the design does not fix, and puts the real point (where the check ran) second. Lead with the placement of the check.

results.quote: the Golf's removal arrived 26 hours after the sale
results.finding: Single reader (B8): a new fact about the Golf case appears outside the scene and the replay. Not confusing; minor.

Every term on audience.does_not_know is given where first used: conversation, lead, lead routing and connection (Concepts), DMS ('dealer management system (DMS)'), ADF XML (delivery table), Rightmove's Real Time Datafeed ('the API through which UK agency software exchanges data with Rightmove'), pull versus push and exactly-once on a lead ID (p48 and table), hot partitions, per-participant inbox index, idempotency keys (p26-p27), GDPR legitimate interest and the EECC 'interpersonal communications service' (p36). Terms the flow readers met unexplained (Keybridge, Common Ground, Lyon apartment, 'sharing platforms, not products', search's peak-to-average ratio) are on audience.already_knows or are used across earlier chapters of the book; the March 2027 neutrality decision is explained in its own clause.

The opening hooks with a direct statement (search, ranking and alerts exist to produce one event), bridges to the two objects, places the chapter in Part VI and gives a concrete roadmap; no dictionary opener, throat-clearing or vague 'this chapter explores'.
p75 does not restate the sections or add new material; it answers the scene's two questions with one design move and states the consequence; p76 hands off with the Safe Deal link.

p75 synthesises ('keep the conversation and the lead apart, and give each its own control') and answers so-what ('A platform that merges the two objects can neither stop a phishing link in time nor defend an invoice; one that keeps them apart can share one conversation service across brands and put a price on the lead').

p75 calls back to the opening claim ('The conversation is where the platform still sees both parties') and to both scene cases (Femke's check before delivery; the Golf's 23 contacts into 19 leads read by Veldmark and Autohaus Ruhrblick); p76 calls back to the Safe Deal phishing link.

The opening-only reader predicted, in order: the two Veldmark cases, definitions of contact/conversation/lead, contact channels, the contact path with the synchronous safety gate, leads through creation, routing, delivery and attribution, retention per data class for messages and leads, the replay of both cases under the 2027 design, trade-offs, vertical differences, failure modes, the Chief Architect's view and review questions. That is every promise of the post spec's roadmap (introduction.roadmap and p04) in its order, with retention after attribution. The evidence prediction (dated engineering posts and investor filings from OLX, Discord, Rightmove, Autotrader, CarGurus, Zillow, CoStar, Adevinta; EU law; fictional Veldmark) matches.

AC-2: the reader predicts the sections the chapter actually has, in their order, and the kinds of evidence, and also why the chapter opens Part VI and what it leaves to neighbouring chapters. The only mismatch with AC-2's expected text is that the expected text is stale: it still names 'the public record' as a section and puts retention before leads, while the chapter has no public-record section (its evidence moved into Contact Channels and the Chief Architect's View) and the post spec's roadmap puts retention after attribution. Judged against the chapter as it is, the criterion is met; the expected text should be updated in the spec (and journal spec) by the author.

AC-1: the reader places the check on the delivery path between stored and shown as a synchronous gate with a 150 ms p99 budget, four verdicts (deliver, deliver with warning, withhold, block), fail-closed for links and payment details from accounts under 24 hours, withholding the bike's link on domain age, with slower asynchronous scoring withdrawing messages and warning counterparties. For the count, it gives one versioned creation and deduplication rule across channels (calls and bookings included), a stable lead ID in one lead contract, and push delivery acknowledged by the CRM per lead ID, turning 23 contacts into the same 19 leads on both sides. Matches expected.

AC-4: the reader says counting the chat store conflates two objects with different owners and lifecycles, misses calls and bookings, has no deduplication or shared lead ID, and makes every chat change alter billing retroactively; builds a separate lead service with its own store, a versioned owned creation rule and a stable lead ID. For the warehouse: only the conversation service stores message content because every copy has to be found, secured and deleted; send message events with identifiers and timings, not text. Matches expected.

AC-5: the reader tells the vendor it is on a pull contract that, as Rightmove's specification describes, delivers leads at least once and often twice by design, so the vendor deduplicates on the stable lead ID; the dealer group gets push by webhook/API, retried until acknowledged with the same lead ID, so the portal owns the duplicates. It does not say in so many words that both are adapters on one versioned lead contract, but that is a supporting point and the criterion (a delivery style for each and who deduplicates) is fully met.
